instruction: I have a list of Hong Kong restaurants that I want to research. Please search for each restaurant on Google Maps and populate my Excel spreadsheet with their information - specifically their address, phone number, and website. Fill in all available fields for each restaurant.

metadata.explanation: This variation counts the total number of filled cells in the data range (A2:D6 = 20 cells total). The evaluator checks that all 20 cells are filled, providing proportional credit (0.05 per filled cell).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator only checks quantity (cells filled) but not quality/correctness of data
Instruction requires specific data types: address, phone number, website - evaluator doesn't validate these
Cannot distinguish between correct Google Maps research data vs. random text filling cells
Any non-empty string in cells would pass - no semantic validation of content
Instruction says 'search for each restaurant on Google Maps and populate' - evaluator cannot verify the research step was performed
Missing validation that columns contain appropriate data types (addresses look like addresses, phones like phones, URLs like websites)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add content validation: check if address column contains location-like text (street names, city)
Add phone number format validation: check if phone column matches phone number patterns
Add website URL validation: check if website column contains valid URLs or domain names
Consider checking if data looks realistic vs. placeholder/random text
Alternative: If only completeness matters, clarify instruction to remove specific field requirements and just say 'fill all cells'
Could add heuristic checks like: phone numbers contain digits and special chars (+, -, parentheses), websites contain domain extensions (.com, .hk, etc.)
